events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts to 75 mph; winds
turn westerly beginning Tuesday evening.

* WHERE...Pribilof Islands.

* WHEN...From 3 AM Tuesday to 9 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds rapidly increase in strength Monday
night/early Tuesday morning and peak late Tuesday morning as a
strong low pressure system moves through the Bering. A short lull
of high winds will occur before a second peak in westerly winds
occurs Tuesday evening through Wednesday morning with winds gusting
to 75 mph. As a result of the long duration of westerly winds, wave
heights of 25 to 30 ft within 15 to 20 nautical miles of Saint Paul
are expected through Wednesday afternoon.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and

gusty through Wednesday.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Northeast to east winds near 20 knots.

* WHERE...Gulf waters beyond 5 fathoms including the Dry
Tortugas.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
swamped bows at reef tract mooring balls, and dragging anchors.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations 6 to 10 inches.

* WHERE...Klondike Highway past milepost 10.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of fronts will push across the

limiting overall snow accumulations.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow and gusty winds expected. Total snow accumulations of 1
to 4 inches, with locally higher totals around 4 to 8 inches for
the Southern Seward Peninsula Coast. Southeast winds could gust as
high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...From 3 AM Wednesday to 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Snow and blowing snow
could reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of
blizzard conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong winds will steadily ramp up Tuesday
night into Wednesday, with snow arriving as winds peak. Rain may
mix with snow at times Wednesday and Thursday as warmer air builds
in out of the south.
